eval_sample.user_input: What is the significance of the SAVE Plan in relation to income-based repayment options and borrower protections?
reference_contexts:
I submitted my annual Income-Driven Repayment ( IDR ) recertification to Aidvantage on time and in full, using the correct process. My income is approximately $ XXXX/year, which is below 150 % of the federal poverty guideline. Under the SAVE Plan or any valid IDR/IBR plan , this income level qualifies for a $ XXXX monthly payment. 

Instead, Aidvantage assigned me a $ XXXX/month paymentan amount that is not legally or mathematically possible based on my income. I contacted them and was placed in a two-month administrative forbearance. After that, they returned with the exact same incorrect payment amount. 

When I pressed for clarification, Aidvantage responded that my IDR application has not been processed yet, even though they had already issued a bill and claimed it was based on a recalculation. Aidvantage has not requested any additional documentation from me. There has been no communication asking for clarification or income verification beyond my original submission.

eval_sample.reference: The context discusses a borrower’s situation with the SAVE Plan, which qualifies for a specific monthly payment based on income. The borrower’s income is below 150% of the federal poverty guideline, making them eligible for a reduced payment under the SAVE Plan or any valid IDR/IBR plan. The borrower highlights issues with incorrect billing and the need for correction, clarification, and protections against negative credit reporting while disputes are resolved.

eval_sample.user_input: Is 15 U.S.C. 1681i the law that requires credit bureaus to conduct reinvestigations of disputed credit report items?
reference_contexts:
I am writing to formally dispute inaccurate information on my credit report. This dispute is submitted under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), 15 U.S.C. 16811, which requires credit reporting agencies to conduct a reasonable reinvestigation of disputed items.

Recent findings by the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ) have brought to light significant concerns regarding XXXX  and XXXX XXXX failure to conduct proper investigations. Specifically, in a lawsuit filed against XXXX  and XXXX, the CFPB alleges that the company engaged in sham investigations, violating consumer protection laws by failing to meet its obligations under the FCRA.

As per 15 U.S.C. 1681i ( a ) ( 1 ) ( A ), XXXX  and XXXX  is required to conduct a thorough and reasonable reinvestigation of disputed items within 30 days. Furthermore, under 15 U.S.C. 1681i ( a ) ( 5 ), any information found to be inaccurate, incomplete, or unverifiable must be promptly deleted or corrected. Failure to adhere to these requirements constitutes a violation of federal law.

Conduct a thorough reinvestigation of the following disputed accounts or items : EDFinancial Services through 15 accounts totaling {$35000.00}.
eval_sample.reference: Yes, 15 U.S.C. 1681i is part of the Fair Credit Reporting Act (FCRA) that requires credit reporting agencies to conduct a reasonable reinvestigation of disputed items, and mandates that any inaccurate, incomplete, or unverifiable information be promptly deleted or corrected.

eval_sample.user_input: Considering the issues with NelNet's handling of auto-debit setup and the history of misconduct and legal violations associated with the account transfer from XXXX, what steps should a legal compliance officer recommend to ensure that NelNet adheres to federal privacy laws and consumer protection statutes, and how can the institution address potential deceptive practices related to auto-payment records and account transfers?

<1-hop>

I keep setting up auto-debit with NelNet, get confirmation, and then the payments aren't processing. In XXXX of XXXX, XXXX of XXXX, and XX/XX/XXXX I tried to set up auto debit for my loan. I go back in and the website shows I didn't make a payment. I have received multiple confirmations that I have been set up for auto-debit and then NelNet deletes the record. I have a paper letter confirming auto-payment enrollment from XX/XX/XXXX, but the website keeps deleting my payment data. Since auto-payment receives a small discount on the loan payment, I suspect the company of skimming the dollar and change that my payment amount should be reduced by per month. Please assist me in correcting this behavior, so that other borrowers are not informed of an auto-debit only to have these bad actors play games with our loan accounts.

<2-hop>

This account was transferred to Nelnet ( NNI ) from XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ; who had engaged in acts of deception and made numerous errors on the account, as well as having broken numerous consumer protection laws, including the FDCPA, FCRA, TCPA, Indiana Senior Consumer Protection Act, Indiana Deceptive Consumers Sales Act. This occurred in XXXX and XXXX. We then sent letters to Nelnet by Certified Mail ( CM ) several times in XXXX and XXXX, detailing the serious misconduct by XXXX. 

Despite signing for the CM and acknowledging receipt of the written complaint and violations of law, XXXX never responded to the CM, nor provided any answers to the questions raised in the CM. This includes responding promptly to certified mail complaints, correcting errors, and ensuring that deceptive practices—such as deleting valid auto-payment records—are eliminated. Strengthening internal controls and adhering strictly to federal privacy and consumer protection laws will help prevent future violations and restore borrower trust.

eval_sample.user_input: How does the FCRA address the requirement for proper investigation and correction of disputed credit report items, especially in cases involving illegal student loan reporting following the Department of Education's abolishment?
reference_contexts:
<1-hop>

I am writing to formally dispute inaccurate information on my credit report. This dispute is submitted under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), 15 U.S.C. 16811, which requires credit reporting agencies to conduct a reasonable reinvestigation of disputed items.

Recent findings by the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ) have brought to light significant concerns regarding XXXX  and XXXX XXXX failure to conduct proper investigations. Specifically, in a lawsuit filed against XXXX  and XXXX, the CFPB alleges that the company engaged in sham investigations, violating consumer protection laws by failing to meet its obligations under the FCRA.

As per 15 U.S.C. 1681i ( a ) ( 1 ) ( A ), XXXX  and XXXX  is required to conduct a thorough and reasonable reinvestigation of disputed items within 30 days. Furthermore, under 15 U.S.C. 1681i ( a ) ( 5 ), any information found to be inaccurate, incomplete, or unverifiable must be promptly deleted or corrected. Failure to adhere to these requirements constitutes a violation of federal law.

Conduct a thorough reinvestigation of the following disputed accounts or items : EDFinancial Services through 15 accounts totaling {$35000.00}.

Failure to do so, such as continued reporting of unverified student loans or sham investigations, constitutes a violation of federal law under the FCRA, as highlighted by recent CFPB findings and legal actions.
